trajectory_summary: The call opens on a false premise (customer denies the form) and never recovers legitimacy; the rep then spends nearly two minutes debating solar mechanics with a resistant customer instead of pivoting to qualification or a clean exit. The call ends abruptly when the rep discovers a utility-company mismatch, closing the call as a DQ but only after burning time on an unwinnable feature debate.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is 'unknown' — observed_outcome here is dq. The disqualification (Valley Electric not serviced) was knowable early and should have been checked before the multi-minute feature debate, meaning the DQ came too late, not too early.

observed_outcome.quote: Gotcha. So I actually know that we we don't work with Valley Electric anyway. So I'll just take you off my list here. I appreciate your time.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep explicitly disqualifies the lead based on the customer's utility provider not being serviced by Ion, ending the call with no appointment and no next step.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The customer volunteers a $240/month bill figure at 02:46, but the call ends within seconds on a DQ (wrong utility provider) — the rep never had the chance to flip it because the DQ took priority, and the DQ appears legitimate.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked what interested the customer in solar (in fact the customer denied any interest or form submission from the start), so no interest reason was ever solicited or given.

script_coverage.quote: Hi. This is Meg. I'm with Ion.
I've I've got it here for a 1320 Greta Boulevard.
Are you with the Valley Electric? Is that your power provider?

primary_coaching_focus.quote: Are you with the Valley Electric? Is that your power provider?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep spent over two minutes arguing solar mechanics with a resistant, ultimately-disqualified customer before asking the one qualifier (utility provider) that would have ended the call immediately. Front-loading basic verify questions avoids wasted, escalating conversations.

key_moments.quote: How are you doing today? Got no form. I'm in got no form.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer denies recognizing the form immediately, and the rep's recovery ('I've got it here for a 1320 Greta Boulevard') doesn't resolve the legitimacy question — it just restates the address, which the customer also doesn't confirm clearly.

key_moments.quote: Right. Yeah. I'm I'm just curious why that is. All they do is replace your current power bill with something cheaper, so it's saving money every month.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is unsolicited feature-selling ('all they do is...') in response to a flat refusal, rather than a curiosity-creating question about the customer's own bill or usage. This invites exactly the mechanism debate that follows.

key_moments.quote: No. Not at all. I mean, it's replacing your current electric bill.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer's neighbor-anecdote objection is a classic cost-skepticism trigger. Instead of flipping it toward the customer's own bill pain, the rep argues the mechanism directly, which keeps the conversation on the customer's chosen (losing) ground.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Do you know if the solar is covering all of his electric needs or just parts or I don't know.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep admits uncertainty ('or I don't know') on the same neighbor-anecdote thread she had flatly denied two exchanges earlier ('No. Not at all.'). The inconsistency signals the rep was improvising the rebuttal rather than working from a clear framework.
